docs.title: alphavantage-java
docs.text: This library was created to provide a fluent interface for accessing the AlphaVantage API with Java.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: To get started using this library, make sure to get an API Key from Alphavantage's website. Add the library as a dependency to your project

docs.title: Installation
Quick Usage Guide
docs.text:
These five steps summarize how to access data using this library

Step 1. configure the wrapper

Step 2. Select a category

Step 3. Set the parameters for the selected category

Step 4. (Optional) Add response callbacks

Step 5. fetch results

docs.title: 1. Configuring the wrapper
docs.text:
Access to the API is through the AlphaVantage Singleton which is accessed using the static api() method of the class.

Tip

Initialize the singleton with a Config instance once through out your apps lifetime.

Java Kotlin 
Config cfg = Config.builder()
    .key("#&ALPHA10100DEMOKEY")
    .timeOut(10)
    .build();

var cfg = Config.builder()
    .key("#&ALPHA10100DEMOKEY")
    .timeOut(10)
    .build()

Use the config object to initialize the api instance. You will use this object to set your api key and configure the http client.

Warning

Using the wrapper without setting a config or a config key will throw an exception.

Java Kotlin 
AlphaVantage.api().init(cfg);

AlphaVantage.api().init(cfg)

That's it! We're good to go.

docs.title: 2. Selecting a category
docs.text:
Here, we choose which data category/endpoint we want to access

Info

Each of category is exposed through a method call in the instantiated wrapper.

Category Method Stock Time Series Data .timeSeries() Forex Rate Data .forex() Exchange Rate Data .exchangeRate() Digital Currency Data .crypto() Technical Indicator Data .indicator() Sector Performance Data .sector() Fundamental Data .fundamentalData() Global Market Status .marketStatus() Ticker/Symbol Search .search()

For example, to select the Stock Time Series:

Java Kotlin 
AlphaVantage.api()
    .timeSeries()

AlphaVantage.api()
    .timeSeries()

docs.title: 3. Setting the parameters for the selected category
docs.text:
To set the api request parameters, call the appopriate parameter methods. For instance for the function parameter function you call daily() for the TIME_SERIES_DAILY function, intraday() for the TIME_SERIES_INTRADAY, and so on.

Let's select the TIME_SERIES_INTRADAY function

Java Kotlin 
AlphaVantage.api()
    .timeSeries()
    .intraday()

AlphaVantage.api()
    .timeSeries()
    .intraday()

Tip

Start setting parameters by calling an appropriate function method in the selected category

docs.title: 4. Adding response callbacks
docs.text:
To handle responses add the onSuccess() or onFailure() async callbacks. Starting from version 1.5.0, this is an optional step.

Java Kotlin 
public void handleSuccess(TimeSeriesResponse response) {
    plotGraph(reponse.getStockUnits());
}
public void handleFailure(AlphaVantageException error) {
    /* uh-oh! */
}

AlphaVantage.api()
    .timeSeries()
    .intraday()
    .forSymbol("IBM")
    .interval(Interval.FIVE_MIN)
    .outputSize(OutputSize.FULL)
    .onSuccess(e->handleSuccess(e))
    .onFailure(e->hanldeFailure(e))
    ...

fun handleSuccess(response:TimeSeriesResponse) {
    plotGraph(reponse.getStockUnits())
}
fun handleFailure(error:AlphaVantageException) {
    /* uh-oh! */
}        

AlphaVantage.api()
    .timeSeries()
    .intraday()
    .forSymbol("IBM")
    .interval(Interval.FIVE_MIN)
    .outputSize(OutputSize.FULL)
    .onSuccess({ e-> handleSuccess(e) })
    .onFailure({ e-> hanldeFailure(e) })            
    ...

Info

Callbacks are optional, you can choose to handle either or both

docs.title: 5. fetch results
docs.text:
When you are okay with setting the parameters call the fetch() method. Simple!

Java Kotlin 
AlphaVantage.api()
    .timeSeries()
    .intraday()
    .forSymbol("IBM")
    .interval(Interval.FIVE_MIN)
    .outputSize(OutputSize.FULL)
    .onSuccess(e->handleSuccess(e))
    .onFailure(e->hanldeFailure(e))
    .fetch();

AlphaVantage.api()
    .timeSeries()
    .intraday()
    .forSymbol("IBM")
    .interval(Interval.FIVE_MIN)
    .outputSize(OutputSize.FULL)
    .onSuccess({ e-> handleSuccess(e) })
    .onFailure({ e-> hanldeFailure(e) })
    .fetch()

From v1.5.0 up, you can also use the synchronous fetch method by calling the fetchSync() method without callback handlers.

Java Kotlin 
TimeSeriesResponse response = AlphaVantage.api()
    .timeSeries()
    .intraday()
    .forSymbol("IBM")
    .interval(Interval.FIVE_MIN)
    .outputSize(OutputSize.FULL)
    .fetchSync();

TimeSeriesResponse response = AlphaVantage.api()
    .timeSeries()
    .intraday()
    .forSymbol("IBM")
    .interval(Interval.FIVE_MIN)
    .outputSize(OutputSize.FULL)
    .fetchSync()

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file. The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Support for realtime bulk quotes
  • Support for crypto intraday
  • Support for global market status
  • Support for symbol search

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Intraday stock time series: added extended_hours, month and adjusted parameters
  • Updated build dependencies
  • Updated outdated Crypto fields to match API responses

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text: • indicator interface in favour of technicalIndicator for accessing Technical Indicators

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Array index out of bounds exception caused by empty API response

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Bid Rates and Ask Rates for Exchange Rates

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Incorrect mapping of time series data
  • Getters for Crypto and Forex Units

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Support for Time Series Data
  • Support for Forex Data
  • Support for Crypto Currencies
  • Support for Exchange Rates
  • Tests for Time Series
  • README

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
public class Config extends Object

Defines configuration parameters you can set for the library to use. You can set the httpClient for the library or use the default httpClient.

HttpLoggingInterceptor loggingInterceptor = new HttpLoggingInterceptor();
loggingInterceptor.level(Level.BASIC);

OkHttpClient client = new OkHttpClient.Builder()
    .connectTimeout(4, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
    .callTimeout(4, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
    .addInterceptor(loggingInterceptor)
    .addInterceptor(mockInterceptor)
    .build();

Config config = Config.builder()
    .key("demo")
    .httpClient(client)
    .build();

//OR: use default http client

Config config = Config.builder()
    .key("demo")
    .build()
